questions.question: Meridian keeps policy PDFs and Word files in Azure Blob Storage and wants Foundry IQ to read them without a separate index. In the course's classification of knowledge sources, which kind is this?
answers: A direct source
An indexed source
A real-time source
A federated source
questions.explanation: Direct sources are raw files read without a separate index, such as Azure Blob Storage and OneLake. Indexed sources are pre-processed into an Azure AI Search index, and real-time sources, such as the Web and SharePoint remote, are queried live at answer time.

questions.question: A knowledge base only helps if the agent actually uses it. Which three behaviors should effective retrieval instructions specify?
answers: Which index to query, the chunk size, and the embedding model
When to retrieve, how to cite, and what to do when unsure
When to retrieve, which reranker to use, and the answer length
How to cite, which tool to call first, and when to hand off
questions.explanation: The course lists three behaviors: when to retrieve (always search before answering), how to cite (a fixed attribution format), and what to do when unsure (a fixed fallback). The lab's policy agent uses rules such as 'ALWAYS search the knowledge base' and a fixed sentence that points to the travel desk.

questions.question: When you create a knowledge base in Foundry IQ, the retrieval reasoning effort is left at Minimal. What does Minimal do?
answers: Sends the question as it is, with no extra model calls: fast and cheap
Lets the model rewrite the question into sub-queries and search more than once
Returns only the matching passages, so that the agent writes the answer itself
Skips the embeddings and matches the uploaded files by keywords only
questions.explanation: Minimal sends the question as it is, with no extra model calls. Low and medium let the model rewrite the question, split it into sub-queries and search more than once; returning the matching passages is the separate output mode, extractive data.

questions.question: Meridian publishes version 3 of its travel agent, and the Teams app keeps working without any reconfiguration. Which property of the Agent Application explains this?
answers: The agent identity, which is separate from the development project
User data isolation, which keeps each user's interactions private
The dedicated invocation URL, which stays the same as new versions are published
The Azure Bot Service, which stores a manifest for each version
questions.explanation: Publishing creates an Agent Application with a dedicated invocation URL, an agent identity and user data isolation. The invocation URL is a stable endpoint across versions, so channels and apps never need reconfiguring when you publish an update.

questions.question: In Demo 4, you publish meridian-docs-helper to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot and choose People in your organization in the publish options. What happens next?
answers: The agent is available to everyone right away, under Your agents
Foundry creates a new invocation URL for the organization channel
Your Microsoft 365 admin reviews the request and assigns access
The preview web app link is shared with every user in the tenant
questions.explanation: With Just you, the agent is available to you right away; with People in your organization, your Microsoft 365 admin reviews the request and assigns access. This matches the organization scope in the lecture, which requires admin approval and lists the agent under Built by your org.

questions.question:
In the refund workflow lab, what does draft contain after this code runs?

```python
workflow = (WorkflowBuilder(start_executor=triage, output_from=[approver])
            .add_edge(triage, policy).add_edge(policy, approver).build())
result = await workflow.run(request)
draft = result.get_outputs()[-1].text
```
answers: The triage classification, because triage is the start executor
The approver's short decision draft for the manager, with a recommendation
The policy agent's refund, because policy is the last edge's source
The joined answers of all three agents, in the order that they ran
questions.explanation: output_from=[approver] makes the approver's answer the output of the workflow, and the last output is the draft that the script prints. It gives the booking, the refund amount, the policy clause and a recommendation, APPROVE or REVIEW, before a manager decides.

questions.question:
In this Agent Framework variant, the second run does not know which booking "it" refers to. Which change fixes it, as done in the lab?

```python
agent = Agent(client=client, name="TravelAgent",
              instructions="Look the booking up before changing it.",
              tools=[get_booking, change_booking])
r1 = await agent.run("What is on MT-51877?")
r2 = await agent.run("Move it to 2026-07-11.")
```
answers: Add the booking reference format to the get_booking docstring
Pass conversation=conversation.id to each run, as in the Responses API labs
Add a @tool function that keeps the last booking ID in a global variable
Create session = agent.create_session() and pass session=session to both runs
questions.explanation: In the Agent Framework, a session keeps the conversation across turns. The lab creates it with agent.create_session() and calls agent.run(text, session=session), so the follow-up knows which booking was meant without repeating the reference.

questions.question: A complex, open-ended problem needs an orchestrator that plans, delegates and adapts, with no fixed order of agents. Which Agent Framework orchestration pattern fits?
answers: Magentic
Group chat
Handoff
Concurrent
questions.explanation: Magentic uses an orchestrator that plans, delegates and adapts with no fixed order, for complex open-ended problems. Group chat shares one conversation for brainstorming, handoff transfers control by expertise, and concurrent runs independent agents in parallel for speed.

questions.question:
Why does the trip planner lab pass all three agents to output_from?

```python
workflow = SequentialBuilder(participants=[flights, hotel, policy],
                             output_from=[flights, hotel, policy]).build()
result = await workflow.run("Plan Lisbon from London, 14 to 16 May 2026, 2 people, budget 1,800 EUR.")
for response in result.get_outputs():
    for msg in response.messages:
        print(f"\n[{msg.author_name}] {msg.text}")
```
answers: So every specialist's answer is an output, and each step prints with its agent's name
So the three agents run in parallel instead of one after the other
So each agent can call the tools that belong to the other agents
So the policy agent receives only the hotel agent's final answer
questions.explanation: SequentialBuilder runs the participants in order, and each agent sees the conversation so far. Listing all three in output_from makes every specialist's answer an output, so the script can print each step with msg.author_name.

questions.question: Meridian's booking agent is live. The team wants evaluations to keep watching it in production so that regressions are caught early. Which option does the course point to?
answers: A one-time evaluation with the full conversations scope
A larger synthetic dataset, regenerated before each release
Tracing with enable_sensitive_data switched on in production
A recurring evaluation, which keeps evaluating the agent in production
questions.explanation: In the portal's evaluation setup, a one-time run checks a version once, while a recurring evaluation keeps watching the agent in production to catch regressions. The lecture adds that evaluations can run continuously on sampled production traffic; recording sensitive data in traces is for development only.

questions.question: After running traced_agent.py, you open Logs in the Application Insights resource and query the agent framework dependency spans. Which field lets you follow one run from the first model call to the last tool call?
answers: The duration of the invoke_agent span for the run
The operation ID shared by all the spans of the run
The conversation ID returned by the Responses API
The connection string attached to the Foundry project
questions.explanation: All the spans of one run share the same operation ID, so you can follow one conversation across the invoke agent span, the chat calls and the execute tool span. The durations then show where the time goes: in the model calls, not in the get_booking tool.

questions.question: In Demo 1, meridian-hotel-analyst gets Code Interpreter to analyse Meridian's partner hotels. Where in the portal do you attach hotels.csv so that the agent's code can read it?
answers: Under Knowledge, by creating a new knowledge base
On the Code Interpreter row under Tools, by adding a file
On the YAML tab, by adding the file path to the definition
In the instructions, by pasting the CSV content as text
questions.explanation: After switching on Code Interpreter under Tools, you add the file on the Code Interpreter row, and it becomes available to the code that the agent writes. After saving, the YAML tab lists the code interpreter tool and the file that it can read.

questions.question: You connect the Microsoft Learn MCP server from the tool catalog to meridian-docs-helper. When you ask a question, the playground asks you to approve each call. Why?
answers: The Learn MCP endpoint needs a sign-in for every call
The agent has no web search tool, so calls are escalated
Catalog tools stay in preview until an admin approves them
A remote MCP tool needs approval by default
questions.explanation: A remote MCP tool requires approval by default, so the playground asks you to approve each call. The Microsoft Learn endpoint itself needs no authentication; in code, require_approval set to "never" or "always" controls this behavior.

questions.question: Meridian is choosing which Azure Language features to build a long-term inbox pipeline on. Which feature is scheduled to retire on 31 March 2029, with a generative model and a prompt as its successor?
answers: Custom named entity recognition (custom NER)
Text Analytics for health
Entity linking
PII detection and redaction
questions.explanation: Five Language features continue long term: language detection, named entity recognition, PII detection, custom NER and Text Analytics for health. Entity linking is one of the eight features that retire on 31 March 2029, together with sentiment analysis, key phrase extraction, summarization, conversational language understanding, custom question answering, custom text classification and orchestration workflow.

questions.question:
In lab part 1, the inbox is analyzed in batches:

```python
client = TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint=os.environ["LANGUAGE_ENDPOINT"],
                             credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
result = client.detect_language(batch)
```

Which expression returns the two-letter language code (for example pt) of the first document in the batch?
answers: result[0].primary_language.iso6391_name
result.primary_language[0].iso6391_name
result[0].detected_language.language
result[0].language.iso_code_name
questions.explanation: Every Text Analytics method takes a list of documents and returns one result per document, so you index the result first. primary_language.iso6391_name holds the ISO code that the lab writes to the CSV file. detected_language.language belongs to the Translator translate results, not to TextAnalyticsClient.

questions.question: In the Foundry portal, under Build > Services, you open the Azure Language playground. Which task is NOT in its type list, so lab part 1 calls it from code instead?
answers: Language detection
Text PII redaction
Text Analytics for health
Named entity recognition
questions.explanation: The Language playground type list offers language detection, three kinds of PII redaction (text, documents and conversations) and Text Analytics for health. Named entity recognition and sentiment analysis are not in this playground; lab part 1 calls them with TextAnalyticsClient.

questions.question: An insurer's claims agent uses the Language MCP server to redact patient identifiers before a claim is filed. Why does the course stress that the Language tool results are deterministic?
answers: The agent's final reply is always worded the same way for the same claim
The same input always gives the same output, which matters for compliance
The model no longer chooses a tool; the MCP server routes each request
Foundry caches the tool results, so repeated calls are never billed
questions.explanation: The lecture states that the Language tool result is deterministic: the same input always gives the same output, and this matters for compliance. Lab part 2.3 adds that the agent's wording may change from run to run, but the detected language and the redaction do not. The model still chooses which tool to call.

questions.question:
The inbox agent attaches the Language MCP server like this:

```python
language = MCPTool(server_label="azure-language",
                   server_url=LANGUAGE_MCP,
                   project_connection_id=os.environ["LANGUAGE_CONNECTION_ID"],
                   require_approval="never")
```

Compliance now asks that a person reviews and approves every Language call before it runs. What do you change?
answers: Remove project_connection_id, so each call asks the user to sign in
Set server_label="approval", so the portal lists each call for review
Set require_approval="always" on the MCPTool
Point server_url at a local Language server hosted from GitHub
questions.explanation: require_approval="never" lets the agent call the Language tools without a human check; "always" makes you review and approve each call before it runs. The project connection only tells Foundry how to sign in, and a self-hosted server changes only the address.

questions.question: In lab part 2.1, the Azure Language in Foundry Tools connection signs in with Microsoft Entra and the project managed identity. Which role assignment do you make in the Azure portal first?
answers: Cognitive Services User on the Foundry resource, for the project's managed identity
Storage Blob Data Contributor on the storage account, for your own user account
Cognitive Services User on the resource group, for your own user account only
Owner on the Foundry project, for the Azure Language MCP server itself
questions.explanation: On the Foundry resource, under Access control, you add Cognitive Services User and choose Managed identity as the member, selecting the project's identity. This role lets an identity call the AI services of the resource, like Language, but not manage it. Storage Blob Data Contributor is used later, in lab part 5, for the audio blobs.

questions.question: In the agent playground, you add the Azure Language MCP server from the tool catalog. You want the agent to call only language detection and PII redaction. Where do you set this?
answers: In the agent instructions, by listing the Language features it must not use
In the approval setting, by choosing Never auto-approve for the tool
On the YAML tab, by replacing the server address with two new tools
In the Allowed tools field of the Language MCP tool configuration
questions.explanation: The Allowed tools field limits which Language features the agent may call; left empty, it allows all of them. The approval setting controls human review (Never auto-approve pauses each call until a person approves it), not which tools are available.

questions.question: Which Meridian requirement points to Azure Speech rather than to gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-tts?
answers: Transcribe a folder of recorded voicemails in a nightly batch job
Read a gate code character by character, with SSML, at a live kiosk
Speak a reply in a warm, unhurried tone set by a plain-text instruction
Bias the spelling of booking references in an uploaded audio file
questions.explanation: The rule from the course: use the generative models when a file goes in, text or speech comes out, and the tone is set by instruction. Use Azure Speech for real-time microphone streaming, fine control with SSML, custom voices or on-device recognition. A live kiosk that spells a gate with say-as needs both real-time recognition and SSML.

questions.question:
The voicemail batch transcribes each file like this:

```python
with audio_path.open("rb") as audio:
    heard = audio_client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-transcribe", file=audio,
        prompt="Travel bookings, references like MT-48213, Portuguese and German names").text
```

What does the prompt argument do?
answers: It sets the transcript language, so every transcript comes back in English
It tells the chat model how to reply to the caller after transcription
It sets the tone instructions that gpt-4o-mini-tts uses for the reply
It primes the model with expected vocabulary, so references are spelled right
questions.explanation: The optional prompt tells the transcription model what vocabulary to expect, so a booking reference such as MT-48213 stays intact. The reply is drafted in a separate responses.create call, and the tone instructions belong to audio.speech.create with gpt-4o-mini-tts.

questions.question: Meridian must transcribe thousands of recorded calls that are already stored in Blob Storage. Which speech to text mode of Azure Speech fits best?
answers: Real-time recognition from a microphone or audio stream
Fast transcription, one synchronous call for each file
Batch transcription, an asynchronous job over files in storage
Custom speech, trained on a sample of the call recordings
questions.explanation: Real-time recognition is for a microphone or stream, fast transcription returns one file in a synchronous call, and batch transcription is an asynchronous job over many files in Blob Storage, started from code or the REST API. Custom speech improves accuracy on your vocabulary; it is not a way of delivering the audio.

questions.question: In the Speech playground, a British English voicemail is transcribed with Faro as Pharaoh, and the booking reference comes out as a date. What does the demo do to fix this?
answers: Adds Faro and the booking reference to a phrase list, and runs it again
Switches the input from the uploaded file to the live microphone
Changes the recognition language from British English to Portuguese
Opens the voice gallery and picks a different British neural voice
questions.explanation: A phrase list tells the recognizer which words to expect, just like the prompt of gpt-4o-transcribe in the lab. The voice gallery belongs to text to speech and does not affect recognition.

questions.question:
To switch the kiosk to Portuguese, you change only the speech config:

```python
speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "pt-PT"
speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "pt-PT-RaquelNeural"

SSML = """<speak version="1.0" xml:lang="en-GB"
    xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/synthesis"
    xmlns:mstts="http://www.w3.org/2001/mstts">
  <voice name="en-GB-SoniaNeural">
    <mstts:express-as style="friendly">{text}</mstts:express-as>
  </voice>
</speak>"""
synthesizer.speak_ssml_async(SSML.format(text=escape(answer.output_text))).get()
```

The Portuguese answers are still spoken by Sonia. Why?
answers: The recognizer must be recreated before a new synthesis voice applies
The SSML document names its own language and voice, so it must change too
escape() converts the Portuguese answer to English before it is spoken
Portuguese voices need the cheerful express-as style instead of friendly
questions.explanation: speak_ssml_async renders the SSML document, and its speak element declares the language while its voice element picks the voice. In lab part 4.3 the trainer changes the language and voice in both places; otherwise Sonia reads the Portuguese answer. escape() only protects the XML from characters such as & or <.

questions.question: Which practice follows the course's security rules for the keys and SAS URLs used by the Speech MCP server?
answers: Create one SAS for the whole storage account with a long expiry, so the tool never breaks
Paste the Foundry resource key into the agent instructions, so the tool can sign in
Commit the container SAS URL to source control, so teammates can reuse the connection
Use the shortest practical SAS expiry, scope each SAS to one container, and rotate keys
questions.explanation: Keys and SAS URLs are secrets: never paste them into prompts, chat transcripts, screenshots or source control. Use the shortest practical SAS expiry, scope a SAS to a single container, and rotate the keys. In the lab, the key and the container SAS URL are stored in the project connection, never in code.

questions.question:
Before calling the voice agent, the lab builds a link to the voicemail:

```python
service = BlobServiceClient(account_url=os.environ["STORAGE_ACCOUNT_URL"],
                            credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
expiry = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=1)
key = service.get_user_delegation_key(datetime.now(timezone.utc), expiry)
sas = generate_blob_sas(service.account_name, os.environ["AUDIO_CONTAINER"], "voicemail_0412.mp3",
                        user_delegation_key=key, permission=BlobSasPermissions(read=True),
                        expiry=expiry)
```

What does this code produce?
answers: A keyless, read-only token for one blob, valid for one hour, signed with an Entra-issued key
A read-write SAS for the whole audio container, signed with storage account key one
A project connection ID that the MCPTool uses to sign in to Blob Storage
An upload of voicemail_0412.mp3 into the audio container, overwriting old copies
questions.explanation: get_user_delegation_key asks Microsoft Entra ID for a signing key, so no storage account key is involved. generate_blob_sas then signs a token for a single blob with read permission only, until the one-hour expiry; the agent receives only this link, never the audio itself.

questions.question: Meridian connects Voice Live to its telephone system. Besides PCM16, which input audio format does Voice Live accept that matches what telephony systems produce?
answers: MP3 audio, at the bit rate of the original call
M4A audio, the format of the stored voicemails
G.711 audio, in mu-law or A-law encoding
WAV files, read from a container SAS URL
questions.explanation: Voice Live streams audio in and out over one WebSocket as PCM16 or as G.711 mu-law and A-law, which is what telephony systems produce. It does not read files from storage; that pattern belongs to the Speech MCP server.

questions.question: You test a voice agent in the agent playground on a laptop without headphones, and the agent keeps hearing its own voice through the speakers. Which setting addresses this?
answers: Automatic turn detection, with a longer silence period
Audio enhancement, with noise suppression and echo cancellation
The avatar, streamed over WebRTC in sync with the voice
A high-definition voice instead of a standard neural voice
questions.explanation: Under the voice and advanced settings, audio enhancement with noise suppression and echo cancellation stops the agent from hearing itself on laptop speakers. Automatic turn detection only decides when the caller has finished speaking.

questions.question:
The phone agent sets up its Voice Live session like this:

```python
await conn.session.update(session=RequestSession(
    modalities=[Modality.TEXT, Modality.AUDIO],
    instructions="You are Meridian's phone assistant. Keep answers under three sentences.",
    voice=AzureStandardVoice(name="en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural"),
    input_audio_format=InputAudioFormat.PCM16,
    turn_detection=ServerVad(silence_duration_ms=500)))
```

What does turn_detection=ServerVad(silence_duration_ms=500) do?
answers: The client stops sending microphone audio after 500 ms of silence
The agent waits 500 ms before it plays each chunk of the reply
The session closes the WebSocket when the caller is silent for 500 ms
The service ends the caller's turn after half a second of silence
questions.explanation: Server VAD is turn detection on the server: a turn ends after half a second of silence, so the service, not your code, decides when the caller has finished. The app keeps streaming the microphone into the input audio buffer the whole time.

questions.question:
The speech translation lab ends like this:

```python
cfg = speechsdk.translation.SpeechTranslationConfig(token_credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
                                                    endpoint=RESOURCE)
cfg.speech_recognition_language = "pt-PT"
for lang in ("en", "de"):
    cfg.add_target_language(lang)
# ... recognize once, then:
synthesizer.speak_text_async(result.translations["en"]).get()
```

Why does it speak the English translation with a separate SpeechSynthesizer instead of event-based synthesis?
answers: A TranslationRecognizer cannot use a token credential together with a voice
Event-based synthesis supports key authentication only, not Entra ID
Event-based synthesis works with a single target language, and there are two
result.translations holds audio bytes that must be decoded before playback
questions.explanation: Event-based synthesis (a voice name on the translation config plus the synthesizing event) works only with a single target language. Manual synthesis passes the translated text to a SpeechSynthesizer, works for any number of targets, and gives full control. result.translations is a dictionary of text, keyed by target language.

questions.question: In the Translator playground, you switch the model from Azure MT to the gpt-5.4-mini language model. What changes, as shown in the demo?
answers: The configuration offers a tone, and the cost is per token instead of per character
The playground can now translate into several target languages in one run
Auto-detect is switched off, so you must choose the source language first
A custom model ID field appears, so a Custom Translator model can plug in
questions.explanation: With a language model, the configuration offers a tone, and the translation is flexible but not deterministic and priced per token. Azure MT gives a faithful, deterministic translation priced per character. The custom model ID belongs to the advanced settings of the Translator itself, and the playground translates to one target at a time.

questions.question: Which statement about customizing Azure Speech and Translator with your own data is correct?
answers: A custom speech model covers every locale of the Foundry resource at once
Custom neural voice is limited access: you apply, and the voice talent records consent
Custom Translator trains on a single-language corpus of about a thousand sentences
Custom NER is trained in the Language playground by pasting a few examples
questions.explanation: Both custom neural voice types, professional and personal, are limited access: you apply, Microsoft reviews the use case, and the voice talent records a consent statement. A custom speech model belongs to one locale, Custom Translator needs parallel documents (at least ten thousand sentences) or a dictionary, and custom NER is a Language project with labeled documents in Blob Storage.

questions.question: Meridian deploys Phi-4-multimodal-instruct from the Foundry catalog to read photos of damaged luggage. How must the request with the photo be shaped?
answers: Responses API, with a developer message and an input_image part that holds a plain string URL
Responses API, with the photo sent as a separate user turn before the question
Chat Completions, with a system message and an image_url part that nests the URL in an object
Chat Completions, with the photo's data URL placed inside the system message
questions.explanation: Open models such as Phi-4-multimodal-instruct are of type chat completion, so they use Chat Completions: the role system, parts of type text and image_url, and the URL nested in an object. In every API the image travels with the question in one user message, never as a separate turn or in the system message.

questions.question:
In describe_damage.py, which part replaces MISSING_PART so that the photo travels with the question?

```python
response = client.responses.create(
    model=os.environ["MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"],
    input=[
        {"type": "message", "role": "developer",
         "content": "You assess luggage damage claims for Meridian Travel Group."},
        {"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "input_text", "text": "Describe the damage and classify it."},
            MISSING_PART,
        ]},
    ],
)
```
answers: {"type": "input_image", "image_url": data_url}
{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}}
{"type": "input_image", "image_url": {"url": data_url}}
{"type": "image", "data": data_url, "role": "user"}
questions.explanation: The Responses API uses an input_image part whose image_url is a plain string, here the base64 data URL. A type image_url part with a nested url object is the Chat Completions shape, and the other two forms are not used by either API.

questions.question:
describe_damage_chat.py sends the same photo through Chat Completions. Which line prints the model's answer?

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=os.environ["MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"],
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You assess luggage damage claims."},
        {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the damage and classify it."},
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}},
        ]},
    ],
)
```
answers: print(response.output_text)
print(response.output[0].content)
print(response.choices[0].text)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
questions.explanation: With Chat Completions the answer is in choices[0].message.content. output_text is where the Responses API puts the answer; this is one of the four name differences between the two APIs that the course highlights.

questions.question: make_samples.py and hero_image.py build an OpenAI client with a base_url that ends in /openai/v1/, instead of calling project.get_openai_client(). Why?
answers: The project client cannot sign in with DefaultAzureCredential, so a separate client is needed
Image and video models are served on the Foundry resource endpoint, not on the project endpoint
The Images API needs an API key, and only the resource endpoint accepts a key
The project endpoint supports only Chat Completions, so images.generate is not available there
questions.explanation: The lab explains that image and video models are called on the Foundry resource itself, so the client is built from the resource name and ends in /openai/v1/. There is still no key: the api_key is a bearer token provider from DefaultAzureCredential.

questions.question: In Lab 2.1 you deploy the image model in the Foundry portal. Which sequence matches the steps shown?
answers: Build > Services > Content Understanding, choose the image modality, select gpt-image-2, deploy with defaults
Build > Models > Deploy a base model, tick Image to text under Inference tasks, open gpt-image-2, deploy
Azure portal > Foundry resource > Model deployments, search for DALL-E 3, Deploy > Custom settings
Build > Models > Deploy a base model, tick Text to image under Inference tasks, open gpt-image-2, Deploy > Custom settings
questions.explanation: The catalog filter for image generation is the text to image inference task, which lists the GPT-Image and FLUX families. The lab deploys gpt-image-2 with custom settings and the Global Standard type; DALL-E 3 has retired and no longer appears.

questions.question:
hero_image.py generates the Lisbon hero image. Which line saves it as a PNG file?

```python
result = client.images.generate(model=os.environ["IMAGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"],
                                prompt=prompt, n=1, size="1536x1024")
out = ROOT / "out"
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
```
answers: (out / "lisbon-hero.png").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(result.data[0].b64_json))
(out / "lisbon-hero.png").write_bytes(result.data[0].b64_json.encode())
(out / "lisbon-hero.png").write_text(result.output_text)
client.images.download_content(result.id).write_to_file("out/lisbon-hero.png")
questions.explanation: The Images API returns the picture as base64 text in data[0].b64_json, so it must be decoded with base64.b64decode before the bytes are written. Writing the encoded text unchanged gives a broken file, and download_content belongs to the video job pattern.

questions.question: Marketing needs a four-second teaser clip. Which prompt best follows the shot recipe taught in this course?
answers: A full day in Lisbon, from breakfast in Alfama to a fado night, across many places, ending with a happy family
Yellow tram, Alfama, golden hour, tourists, laundry, river, castle, fado, pastries, tiles, sunset, Lisbon
Slow handheld push along a narrow Alfama street at golden hour, laundry overhead, a yellow tram crossing at the end, warm low sun
A beautiful cinematic Lisbon video in warm light, with a caption that shows the itinerary name on screen
questions.explanation: The recipe describes one shot: framing and camera move first, then the subject with concrete details, then a small action, then light and style. A four-second clip holds two or three movements, not a plot, and the lab prompts ask for no text on screen.

questions.question:
teaser_video.py creates a video job and polls it. Which line replaces the TODO line to download the finished clip?

```python
video = client.videos.create(model=os.environ["VIDEO_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"],
                             prompt=shot_prompt, size="1280x720", seconds="4")
while video.status not in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled"):
    time.sleep(20)
    video = client.videos.retrieve(video.id)

if video.status == "completed":
    content = None  # TODO: download the clip
    content.write_to_file("out/lisbon-teaser.mp4")
```
answers: content = client.videos.retrieve(video.id, variant="mp4")
content = client.videos.create(video.id, download=True)
content = client.videos.result(video.id).content
content = client.videos.download_content(video.id, variant="video")
questions.explanation: Video generation is asynchronous: create the job, poll it with retrieve until it is completed, failed or cancelled, then download the content with the video variant. The other calls are not part of that pattern; retrieve only returns the job and its status.

questions.question: On a new Foundry resource, every Content Understanding analyzer fails. Lab 3.1 runs set_defaults.py once per resource first. What does that step do?
answers: It deploys the prebuilt-image, prebuilt-document and prebuilt-audio analyzers to the project
It grants your Entra identity the Cognitive Services User role on the Foundry resource
It maps the model names that analyzers use to your chat and embedding deployments, with update_defaults
It sets one confidence threshold that every analyzer on the resource applies
questions.explanation: Analyzers name models, and the resource maps each name to one of your deployments; on a new resource that map is empty. update_defaults with model_deployments fills it (the chat model and text-embedding-3-large), and the same setting appears in the Content Understanding settings in the portal.

questions.question: The support call analyzer needs the booking reference that the traveler says aloud, and the photo analyzer needs a bed count. Which field method do the labs use for both, and why?
answers: extract, because both values are present in the content and can be copied verbatim
classify, because both values must come from a fixed list of allowed labels
generate, because extract works only on documents, where the value is written down
extract, because only extracted fields return value_string or value_number
questions.explanation: Extract copies a value that is written in the content, so it applies to documents. For a photo or a call nothing is written down, so the labs use generate for BookingReference and BedCount, and classify only where a list of labels exists, such as Reason or RoomType.

questions.question: In the Content Understanding playground of the Foundry portal, you test the Casa do Douro invoice against a prebuilt analyzer. Which choices did Demo 4 make?
answers: Modality document, the procurement analyzer, then Run analysis
Modality image, the image search analyzer, then Run analysis
Modality document, the layout analyzer, then Customize in CU Studio
Modality document, the tax forms analyzer, then the code tab
questions.explanation: Procurement covers invoices and purchase orders. After Run analysis, the left side boxes each value on the page (the grounding) and the right side lists the fields with their confidence; Customize in CU Studio is the path to build a custom analyzer from one sample.

answers: "fieldSchema": {"confidence": True, "fields": {...}}
"baseAnalyzerId": "prebuilt-invoice-confidence"
"models": {"confidence": os.environ["MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"]}
"config": {"estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence": True, "returnDetails": True}
questions.explanation: The config setting estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence turns on the grounding and a confidence score for every extracted field; without it the payment rule has nothing to compare. The lab notes that the lab guide forgot this line, so the code adds it.

questions.question: The Casa do Douro invoice is analyzed: the vendor and the total are found with high confidence, but the due date says "See terms, net 30 days". What does pay_invoices.py do with it?
answers: It schedules the payment, because the generated Summary field explains the payment terms
It routes the invoice to review, because a missing value counts as weak, like a confidence below 0.9
It schedules the payment with a due date that the model generates 30 days after the invoice date
It retries the analysis up to three times until the service returns a due date
questions.explanation: There is no date to copy, so DueDate stays empty, and the rule treats a missing value as weak, the same as a confidence below the 0.9 threshold. The Summary and Category fields never decide a payment, and the three retries only cover an empty contents list.

questions.question: The search service's system-assigned identity holds Storage Blob Data Reader on the storage account. The indexer reads the archive, but writing the knowledge store fails. What is missing?
answers: Search Index Data Contributor on the search service, for your own account
Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor, for the search service identity
Cognitive Services OpenAI User on the Foundry resource, for the search service identity
A move of the search service from the Basic tier down to the Free tier
questions.explanation: The knowledge store writes the enriched output back to the same storage account, so the search identity also needs Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor. Cognitive Services OpenAI User is for the embedding model, and the Free tier has no managed identity at all.

questions.question: Meridian wants the indexer to add fields from the Content Understanding invoice analyzer of section 4 to each archive document. No built-in skill does this. What does the course recommend?
answers: Add an object projection to the knowledge store that calls the analyzer for each file
Add a second data source for Content Understanding next to the Blob Storage source
Mark the target index fields as facetable, so the analyzer fills them at query time
Add a custom skill that calls your own endpoint, typically an Azure Function that calls the analyzer
questions.explanation: When no built-in skill fits, a custom skill calls your own endpoint, typically an Azure Function, and returns fields; calling Content Understanding is the common pattern named in the lecture. Projections only write enriched output to storage, and field attributes do not run any enrichment.

questions.question: With the lab's SearchClient on the meridian-archive index, you want documents that mention Lisbon and also have Porto in the locations collection, plus a count per location. Which call does that?
answers: search.search(search_text="Lisbon", filter="locations eq 'Porto'", facets=["locations"])
search.search(search_text="Lisbon Porto", select=["title", "locations"], top=5)
search.search(search_text="Lisbon", filter="locations/any(l: l eq 'Porto')", facets=["locations"], select=["title", "locations"])
search.search(search_text="Lisbon", facets=["locations eq 'Porto'"], select=["title", "locations"])
questions.explanation: locations is a filterable, facetable collection, so the OData filter uses any to match Porto, as in the search explorer demo, and facets on locations returns the counts through results.get_facets(). Adding Porto to the search text does not restrict the results, and a facet is not a filter.

questions.question: In Demo 1, how is the suitcase claim tested in the Foundry portal chat playground, with no code?
answers: Paste the photo's base64 data URL into the instructions box, then ask the question in the chat box
Paste the claims rule into the instructions box, then attach the photo in the chat box and type the question with it
Upload the photo on the deployment's details page, then ask the question in the chat playground
Attach the photo in the instructions box, then send the claim question as a second message
questions.explanation: The instructions box holds the claims rule (Meridian pays up to 400 euros per bag), and the photo is attached in the chat box together with the question, so both go in one message. Continue in code then shows the matching responses.create call.

questions.question: In Demo 2, the image playground of the gpt-image-2 deployment shows several settings. Which one corresponds to the n parameter of images.generate?
answers: The quality setting under the prompt, with low, medium or high
The number of variations, under parameters
The image format, under parameters
The size setting under the prompt
questions.explanation: Under parameters the playground shows the image format and the number of variations, which is n in code. Size and quality sit under the prompt and map to the size and quality of the same call.

questions.question: In the video playground of the sora-2 deployment, you attach the Lisbon hero image before you generate. What does this do?
answers: The clip starts from that frame, which keeps the scene consistent
The image is laid over the whole clip as a watermark
The playground runs the job as a synchronous call instead
The image replaces the text prompt, which is then ignored
questions.explanation: Demo 3 shows that the attach button takes an image and the clip then starts from that frame, for example the hero image from the lab. Behind the button it is still the same create, poll and download job.

questions.question: In the Azure portal, meridian-archive-indexer shows a failed document in its execution history. Which feature lets you replay that one document through the skillset, step by step?
answers: Debug sessions
Search explorer
The schedule on the indexer's settings tab
The fields tab of the index
questions.explanation: Demo 6 shows that a failed document appears in the execution history, and debug sessions replay one document through the skillset step by step. Search explorer queries the index, the settings tab sets the schedule, and the fields tab shows field attributes.

questions.question: An insurer's claims system must post every new claim to an agent the moment it arrives, with no chat window involved. The triage logic is the insurer's own Python code. Which choice matches the guidance of the course?
answers: A prompt agent with the claims API listed as a tool in its definition
A hosted agent whose container speaks the Invocations protocol
A hosted agent whose container speaks only the Activity protocol
A prompt agent published to Teams so that claims arrive as messages
questions.explanation: Custom orchestration code and a webhook-style trigger are both reasons to choose a hosted agent over a prompt agent. Invocations gives the raw HTTP request and response for webhooks, batch jobs and custom payloads, while Activity is the protocol the platform bridges when an agent is published to Teams.

questions.question: A bank's hosted agent gets no requests overnight, and its sessions use the default idle timeout. At eight in the morning the first customer sends a request in an existing session. What happens?
answers: The platform rebuilds the container image and creates a new agent version for the day
The request fails until an operator restarts the agent from the Foundry portal
A new session starts, and the files the session wrote the day before are lost
The session resumes with its files intact, and no compute was billed while it was idle
questions.explanation: After the idle timeout (fifteen minutes by default) the platform releases the session's compute, so nothing is billed. The next request resumes the session, and its home directory and uploaded files persist across turns.

questions.question:
client/test_local.py talks to the agent running on the laptop:

```python
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8088", api_key="local")
response = client.responses.create(input=text,
                                   previous_response_id=previous_id)
```

Why does the request pass no model parameter?
answers: The agent decides its model; a model name here is passed on as a deployment name and fails
The local host server reads the model name from the api_key value, so it must be left out
previous_response_id already carries the model, so sending it again raises a duplicate error
Model selection is only supported on the hosted endpoint, not on the local host server
questions.explanation: The agent itself is configured with FoundryChatClient and its model deployment, so the client only sends the input and the previous response ID. The script notes that a model name in the request would be passed on as a deployment name and fail with DeploymentNotFound; the local server checks no key.

questions.question: The course insists that every image build gets a unique tag, such as meridian-agent:2 or a pipeline tag, and never latest. What is the reason?
answers: A version points at an exact image, so it must stay reproducible
Azure Container Registry rejects any push that uses the latest tag
The platform only pulls images whose tag is a plain whole number
Unique tags let a new version reuse the session sandboxes of the old one
questions.explanation: An agent version references one exact image, and versions are immutable, so the image behind a version must never change. Unique tags also make it possible to tell which image a version runs, which is what makes a rollback safe.

questions.question:
Here is agent/Dockerfile from the capstone:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.13-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8088
CMD ["python", "main.py"]
```

Which statement about this image is correct?
answers: COPY . . brings in the .env file, which gives the container its project endpoint
main.py runs ResponsesHostServer, which serves /responses and /readiness on port 8088
Port 8088 is only for laptop tests; in Foundry the platform calls the container on port 80
The image must be built on an ARM machine to match the hosted agent runtime
questions.explanation: The same main.py that ran on the laptop ends with ResponsesHostServer(agent).run(), which serves the Responses protocol and the readiness endpoint on port 8088, the port hosted agents listen on. No .env file goes into the image, and the image must be linux/amd64, which az acr build --platform linux/amd64 produces.

questions.question:
deploy/create_version.py registers the image as a new version:

```python
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name=agent_name,
    definition=HostedAgentDefinition(
        container_configuration=ContainerConfiguration(image=image),
        cpu="1", memory="2Gi",
        protocol_versions=[ProtocolVersionRecord(
            protocol=AgentEndpointProtocol.RESPONSES, version="2.0.0")],
        environment_variables=environment,
    ),
)
```

Which statement about this definition is correct?
answers: The agent gets 1 CPU and 2 GiB in total, shared by every session that runs at the same time
The version stays stopped after this call until a separate start call is made on the agent
environment must also contain FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, or the container cannot find its project
Each session sandbox gets 1 CPU and 2 GiB, and Responses 2.0.0 makes the platform pass the user and call IDs
questions.explanation: The CPU and memory apply to each session sandbox, and with protocol version 2.0.0 the platform passes the user and call IDs that the host server needs. There is no separate start step: the script polls get_version until the status is active or failed, and the platform injects FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT itself.

questions.question: In the Foundry portal you open meridian-agent in the Playground. Where can you confirm, without opening the code, which image tag the version runs and which protocol it speaks?
answers: On the Traces tab, where the span tree of each turn starts with the image tag and protocol
In the log stream on the right, which prints the Dockerfile each time a session starts
In the Sessions view, where the files tab of each session lists the image and its tag
In the setup panel's agent info: kind hosted, the code asset, the protocols and the environment variables
questions.explanation: The Playground's setup panel shows the agent info: the kind is hosted, the code asset is the image in the registry (for example meridian-agent:1), the protocols panel lists Responses, and the environment variables are the ones create_version passed in. The log stream shows the container's own output.

questions.question: An airline wants one hosted agent behind three channels: web chat, a baggage scanner that posts a message when it flags a damaged bag, and a phone line that streams audio. Which protocol mapping matches the course?
answers: Web chat: Invocations; scanner: Responses; phone: Activity
Web chat: Activity; scanner: A2A; phone: Invocations over WebSocket
Web chat: Responses; scanner: Invocations; phone: Invocations over WebSocket
Web chat: Responses; scanner: Responses; phone: Invocations
questions.explanation: Responses is the OpenAI-compatible conversation protocol, Invocations carries raw HTTP for webhooks and batch work, and Invocations over WebSocket is full-duplex streaming for voice. One container can serve all three, declared on the version when it is created.

questions.question:
client/chat.py holds a conversation with the hosted agent:

```python
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=os.environ["FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT"],
                          credential=DefaultAzureCredential(), allow_preview=True)
client = project.get_openai_client(agent_name="meridian-agent")

chain = {"previous_response_id": previous_id} if previous_id else {}
response = client.responses.create(input=text, **chain)
previous_id = response.id
```

Which statement about this client is correct?
answers: The script stores every message locally and resends the full history on each new turn
On the first turn no previous_response_id is sent, because the endpoint rejects an empty value
get_openai_client returns a client bound to the model deployment, not to the agent endpoint
allow_preview=True turns on background mode, so each answer must be fetched later by id
questions.explanation: get_openai_client with the agent name returns an OpenAI client bound to the agent's dedicated endpoint, and the platform, not the script, keeps the conversation through previous_response_id. On the first turn there is no ID, and the script sends nothing because a null value is rejected; allow_preview=True only sends the preview opt-in header.

questions.question: A hosted agent misbehaves. According to the lab, where in the Foundry portal do you look to see what the container itself did during a conversation?
answers: The session's log stream and files tab, opened from the Sessions view
The Details tab, under the identity and access section
The Traces tab, by filtering the rows on the agent version
The Playground version picker, by switching to the latest version
questions.explanation: Each row in the Sessions view is a session with its status, agent version and expiry, and opening it shows the log stream with the container's logs and the files the session wrote. The trace tells you what the agent decided; the session log tells you what the container did.

questions.question: A new hosted agent version goes to failed with an image pull error. The image was built with --platform linux/amd64. Which identity and role does the course point to as the usual fix?
answers: The agent identity needs Storage Blob Data Reader on the registry's storage account
The deployer needs Foundry Project Manager on the project before the image can be pulled
The project's managed identity needs Container Registry Repository Reader on the registry
The web app's managed identity needs AcrPush on the registry to pull the new image
questions.explanation: The managed identity of the project resource pulls the container image, so it needs Container Registry Repository Reader on the registry. The two usual causes of a failed version are an image built for the wrong platform and this missing registry role; the deployer's Foundry Project Manager role is needed to create versions, not to pull images.

questions.question: The agent needs a partner API key. Security requires that the key is never in the image, the repository or a plain environment variable, and that rotating it needs no redeploy. What does the course prescribe?
answers: Store it in a Key Vault-backed project connection and reference it with ${{connections.partner-hotels.credentials.key}}
Pass it to az acr build as a build argument so that it is compiled into the agent image
Store it as a GitHub repository variable that create_version.py copies into the definition
Add it to the .env file, which the platform copies into the container when the sandbox starts
questions.explanation: A project connection backed by Key Vault holds the value, and the version's environment variable only references it with the connections placeholder. The value is resolved when the sandbox starts and the API never echoes it back, so a rotated key needs no redeploy; the .env file never goes into the image.

questions.question: Meridian adds a tool to meridian-toolbox by running create_toolbox.py again. What else is needed before the running hosted agent can use the new tool?
answers: Rebuild the image and create an agent version that lists the tool in its definition
Nothing: the new toolbox version becomes the default behind the same MCP endpoint
Write the new versioned toolbox URL into TOOLBOX_ENDPOINT and create a new version
Create a new agent version so that the platform issues a new agent identity for it
questions.explanation: Hosted agents do not list tools in their definition; they reach Foundry tools through one toolbox MCP endpoint. Running the script again creates a new toolbox version and makes it the default, so the endpoint never changes and the agent picks up the new tools with no redeploy.

questions.question:
In agent/main.py, the tools are built like this:

```python
tools = [get_booking, change_booking, describe_damage]

toolbox_endpoint = os.environ.get("TOOLBOX_ENDPOINT")
if toolbox_endpoint:
    tools.append(FoundryToolbox(credential, url=toolbox_endpoint))
```

Version one answered only booking questions; version two also answers archive questions. What changed between the two versions?
answers: main.py was edited to add archive search as a fourth local function tool next to get_booking
The agent definition of version two listed the toolbox tools in its own tools property
create_version.py put TOOLBOX_ENDPOINT into the container environment; the code is the same
FoundryToolbox read a toolbox key from a .env file that was copied into image tag two
questions.explanation: Version two is the same code with a new image tag and TOOLBOX_ENDPOINT in its environment, so main.py adds FoundryToolbox, which connects with the agent identity. One image, and the environment decides what the agent can reach.

questions.question: The Meridian web page on Azure App Service lets travelers chat with the hosted agent. Which design matches the capstone?
answers: The browser calls the agent endpoint directly with an Entra token that the page requests on load
The web app keeps a project API key in its app settings and sends it with every chat request
The web app signs in as the agent identity, which holds Search Index Data Reader on the index
The web app calls the agent endpoint server side with its own managed identity, which holds Foundry User
questions.explanation: On App Service, DefaultAzureCredential resolves to the web app's system-assigned managed identity, and deploy_web.py gives it the Foundry User role. The browser talks only to the web app, so the endpoint and the token stay on the server side and there is no key anywhere.

questions.question:
Part of .github/workflows/ship.yml:

```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  agent:
    steps:
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
```

What does `id-token: write` make possible?
answers: The workflow requests a short-lived GitHub token that Entra ID accepts through a federated credential
The workflow writes a new client secret into the repository variables at the end of each run
The workflow pushes images to the registry without the AcrPush role on the pipeline identity
The workflow creates a fresh Entra app registration for itself on every push to the main branch
questions.explanation: The permission lets the workflow ask GitHub for a short-lived OIDC token, which Entra ID accepts because setup_github_oidc.py created a federated credential for the repository's main branch. No password or client secret exists anywhere, so the client, tenant and subscription IDs are stored as repository variables, not secrets.

questions.question: A traveler reports a wrong booking answer. On the Traces tab of meridian-agent you open that request. Which span do you select first to see which tool ran, with which arguments, and what it returned?
answers: The invoke agent span at the top of the tree
The first chat span, which shows its tokens
The execute tool span for get booking
The second chat span, which wrote the answer
questions.explanation: The span tree shows invoke agent for the whole turn, a chat call that decided to call a tool, execute tool get booking inside the container, and a second chat call that wrote the answer. The tool span's details show the tool, its arguments and the result it returned, which is where you check whether the model called the right tool with the right data.

questions.question: Version three of meridian-agent answers badly, and the fix will take a while. Which action in the Foundry portal makes the web page and the chat client get version two again?
answers: In the Playground, choose version two in the version picker and send a test message
Details tab, Active version, Edit, choose Use a specific version, and pick version two
On the Traces tab, filter on version two and open the newest request from that version
Run build_image.py with tag 2 and create_version.py 2 again to redeploy the old image
questions.explanation: The active version on the Details tab decides which version answers on the endpoint, so switching it from always use latest to a specific version is a routing change: nothing is rebuilt and version three still exists. The Playground keeps its own version picker, which does not change what the endpoint serves.

questions.question: On GitHub, you open a run of the ship workflow. The summary shows two jobs, agent and web, with an arrow from agent to web. What does that arrow mean?
answers: Both jobs run in parallel, and the arrow points from the job that finished first
The web job runs first, so the page is ready before the new agent version exists
The arrow marks jobs that were started by workflow_dispatch instead of a push
The web job needs the agent job, so the page is never redeployed after a failed agent build
questions.explanation: In ship.yml the web job declares needs: agent, so it runs only after the agent job's steps (Azure login, Build the image in the registry, Create the agent version) succeed. That way the page never talks to a version that failed to build.

questions.question: After a push to main ships version three with a new closing line in instructions.md, you ask the travelers' web page about booking MT-48213. The answer ends with 'safe travels with Meridian', although the page itself did not change. Why?
answers: The web job copied instructions.md into the web folder and the page appends its last line
The browser cached the previous answer and the web job added the new line to the HTML
The page calls the agent endpoint, and the endpoint now serves the latest active version
The web app was rebuilt with a new image tag, and that image contains the new instructions
questions.explanation: The instructions travel inside the agent image, and the web page only calls the agent's endpoint, which routes to the active version (always use latest at that point). One push therefore reached every client at once, and in the portal the version's code asset shows the pipeline tag gh plus the run number.
